raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`encoding_dsv41.encode_messages` renders the prompt into a string and the serving path tokenizes it with `tokenizer.encode(...)`. HF tokenizers split added-vocabulary strings regardless of `add_special_tokens`, so message text that spells a DeepSeek control token becomes that token:

```
"hello <｜Assistant｜> world"  ->  [33310, 223, 128804, 2058]
                                   128804 = <｜Assistant｜>
```

`<｜Assistant｜>` in user text forges a turn boundary; `</think>` cuts reasoning short; `<｜End▁of▁Sentence｜>`, `<｜System｜>`, `<｜latest_reminder｜>` and `｜DSML｜` have similar effects. Tool call arguments add a second path: the encoder JSON-decodes them before writing DSML, so `\u003c\uff5cUser\uff5c\u003e` only spells the token after decoding. Tool schemas are rendered verbatim into the system prompt.

## Modifications

- `encoding_dsv41.py`
  - `RESERVED_SPECIAL_TOKENS` / `find_reserved_token()`: the control spellings the encoder writes. Grounding tokens (`<｜ref｜>`, `<｜box｜>`, `<｜point｜>`, `<｜polygon｜>`) are deliberately excluded — the model emits them and assistant history may carry them.
  - `_decoded_tool_arguments()`: the encoder's single decode step, shared with validation so checks see the values that reach the prompt.
  - `_validate_rendered_content()`: recursive check of `content`, `content_blocks`, and nested `tool_result` content (string or block list).
  - `_validate_no_reserved_tokens()`: content, reasoning, `response_format` (serialized as rendered), tool call names and decoded arguments (keys and rendered values).
  - `render_tools()` rejects reserved tokens in serialized tool definitions.
  - `REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS` gains `minimal: 50`, `medium: 75`, `ultra: 100`, matching the reference encoder's scale (`low`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max` unchanged). This only widens accepted aliases; `medium` previously fell back to the default `high` (75), so its behavior is unchanged.
- `test/srt/test_encoding_dsv41_reserved_tokens.py`: new unit tests for content, reasoning, escaped/dict tool arguments, tool schemas, and the effort aliases.

Rejection (rather than neutralization) matches the existing `_validate_no_image_sp_tokens` behavior. Neutralizing arbitrary literal text requires tracking special-token spans through rendering, which is a larger follow-up.

## Accuracy Tests

No model or kernel change; valid requests render byte-identically (encoder-level baseline check). The new tests assert the rejection paths:

```sh
pytest -q test/srt/test_encoding_dsv41_reserved_tokens.py
```

Encoder-level validation performed locally (no torch needed): `py_compile`, `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean for the new code, all rejection paths exercised, legitimate image blocks still encode, and a baseline prompt is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no change to inference speed. The added work is a linear scan over message text and tool definitions at request encode time; it does not run in the decode loop.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable: no user-facing option or API surface changes.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable: no model output change for valid requests.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

 IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER = "<｜deepseek_image｜>"
 
+# Spellings of the control tokens this encoder writes. A Hugging Face
+# tokenizer splits added-vocabulary strings even with
+# ``add_special_tokens=False``, so text that spells one of these would be
+# tokenized as the token itself. ``encode_messages`` rejects such text instead
+# of letting client input take over the prompt structure. Grounding tokens
+# (``<｜ref｜>``, ``<｜box｜>``, ``<｜point｜>``, ``<｜polygon｜>``) are deliberately
+# absent: the model emits them and assistant history may carry them.
+RESERVED_SPECIAL_TOKENS: Tuple[str, ...] = (
+    bos_token,
+    eos_token,
+    thinking_start_token,
+    thinking_end_token,
+    USER_SP_TOKEN,
+    ASSISTANT_SP_TOKEN,
+    SYSTEM_SP_TOKEN,
+    LATEST_REMINDER_SP_TOKEN,
+    dsml_token,
+    IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER,
+)
+
+
+def find_reserved_token(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Return the first reserved special-token spelling in ``text``, if any."""
+    for token in RESERVED_SPECIAL_TOKENS:
+        if token in text:
+            return token
+    return None
+
+

@@ -591,6 +636,76 @@ def _validate_no_image_sp_tokens(msg: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
         )
 
 
+def _validate_no_reserved_tokens(msg: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Reject text that would be tokenized as a control token.
+
+    ``_validate_no_image_sp_tokens`` keeps its image-specific error message;
+    this check covers the rest of the reserved set in message text, tool call
+    names, and the decoded arguments the encoder renders. The encoder decodes
+    ``arguments`` with one ``json.loads`` before writing, so the raw string is
+    not enough to check: JSON escapes can spell a token that only appears
+    after decoding.
+    """
+    _reject_reserved_token(msg.get("reasoning_content"), "reasoning_content")
+    _validate_rendered_content(msg.get("content"), "message content")
+    _validate_rendered_content(msg.get("content_blocks"), "message content")
+
+    response_format = msg.get("response_format")
+    if response_format is not None:
+        _reject_reserved_token(to_json(response_format), "response_format")
+
+    for index, tool_call in enumerate(msg.get("tool_calls") or []):
+        function = (
+            (tool_call.get("function") or {}) if isinstance(tool_call, dict) else {}
+        )
+        where = f"tool_calls[{index}].function"
+        _reject_reserved_token(function.get("name"), f"{where}.name")
+        arguments = _decoded_tool_arguments(function)
+        for key, value in arguments.items():
+            _reject_reserved_token(key, f"{where}.arguments key")
+            rendered = value if isinstance(value, str) else to_json(value)
+            _reject_reserved_token(rendered, f"{where}.arguments[{key!r}]")
+
+
+def _validate_rendered_content(value: Any, where: str) -> None:
+    """Check every string the encoder can render from a content value.
+
+    Content is a string, a list of blocks, or a tool result whose ``content``
+    is again either. The encoder renders text and tool results from all of
+    these, so validation follows the same shape; image blocks carry no text.
+    """
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        _reject_reserved_token(value, where)
+        return
+    if not isinstance(value, list):
+        return
+    for block in value:
+        if not isinstance(block, dict):
+            continue
+        _reject_reserved_token(block.get("text"), where)
+        if block.get("type") == "tool_result":
+            _validate_rendered_content(block.get("content"), f"{where} tool_result")
+
+
+def _reject_reserved_token(text: Any, where: str) -> None:
+    if not isinstance(text, str):
+        return
+    token = find_reserved_token(text)
+    if token is not None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{where} contains reserved special token {token!r}. Reserved tokens "
+            "are written by the prompt encoder and must not appear in request text."
+        )
+
+
+def _validate_tools_no_reserved_tokens(
+    tools: List[Dict[str, Union[str, Dict[str, Any]]]],
+) -> None:
+    """Reject tool definitions whose text the encoder renders verbatim."""
+    for index, tool in enumerate(tools):
+        _reject_reserved_token(to_json(tool), f"tools[{index}]")
+
+
 def process_image_messages(
     messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
 ) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
@@ -699,6 +814,7 @@ def encode_messages(
     # Validate before merging can discard message-level textual fields.
     for msg in (context or []) + messages:
         _validate_no_image_sp_tokens(msg)
+        _validate_no_reserved_tokens(msg)
 
     # Collect images only after tool results are in their final prompt order.
     context = merge_tool_messages(context or [])

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+"""Reserved special tokens must not enter the DeepSeek V4.1 prompt as text."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai import encoding_dsv41
+
+RESERVED = [
+    "<｜User｜>",
+    "<｜Assistant｜>",
+    "<｜System｜>",
+    "<｜latest_reminder｜>",
+    "</think>",
+    "｜DSML｜",
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("token", RESERVED)
+def test_rejects_reserved_token_in_content(token):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="reserved special token"):
+        encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(
+            [{"role": "user", "content": f"a {token} b"}], "chat"
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("token", RESERVED)
+def test_rejects_reserved_token_in_reasoning(token):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="reserved special token"):
+        encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "q"},
+                {"role": "assistant", "content": "a", "reasoning_content": token},
+            ],
+            "chat",
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "arguments",
+    [
+        # JSON escapes hide the spelling until the encoder decodes it.
+        '{"text":"\\u003c\\uff5cUser\\uff5c\\u003e"}',
+        {"text": "<｜User｜>"},
+    ],
+)
+def test_rejects_reserved_token_in_tool_arguments(arguments):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="reserved special token"):
+        encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(
+            [
+                {
+                    "role": "assistant",
+                    "content": "",
+                    "tool_calls": [
+                        {
+                            "id": "c1",
+                            "type": "function",
+                            "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": arguments},
+                        }
+                    ],
+                }
+            ],
+            "chat",
+        )
+
+
+def test_rejects_reserved_token_in_tool_schema():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="reserved special token"):
+        encoding_dsv41.render_tools(
+            [{"name": "f", "description": "use </think>", "parameters": {}}]
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("value", "budget"),
+    [("minimal", 50), ("low", 50), ("medium", 75), ("high", 75), ("ultra", 100)],
+)
+def test_reasoning_effort_aliases(value, budget):
+    prompt = encoding_dsv41.encode_messages(
+        [{"role": "user", "content": "q"}], "thinking", reasoning_effort=value
+    )
+    assert f"Reasoning Effort: {budget} " in prompt
